# Splicing details (demo)

A demo of a new plan export: the **splicing details** of a project's fiber, as a **single line diagram** and as a **detailed** splicing drawing, for **Access OSP** and for **Broadband (OLT / ODN)**. Output: PDF, DXF (R12) or both in one ZIP.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `splice.js` | The engine: fiber assignment, the drawings (A3 sheets), and the writers (SVG preview, PDF, DXF R12, ZIP). No other library needed. |
| `splice-demo.html` | The demo page: made-up samples, editable tables, preview, export. Open it beside `splice.js` (for example `/beta/vendor/splice/splice-demo.html` once it is on the beta website). |
| `splice.html`, `ask.css` | **The app's page** (beta): the Ask & Draw page on the project's own data, opened over G-eSAA from the Drawing (see *In the app* below). `ask.css` is the style of both pages. |
| `ask-demo.html`, `ask.js` | The **Ask & Draw** demo (the plan for the app): five made-up projects shaped like the app's data, a bridge to the engine, the live single line diagram on top and one plain question at a time below, tap-to-change, the fiber strip, As-Plan / As-Built (Mark tested), export. |

Everything in the samples is made up: sites, codes, cable IDs, pole IDs and names.

## What the reference drawings show

These notes come from the owner's reference files (a PowerPoint of Access OSP single line diagrams and two broadband DXFs). The files themselves are confidential and are **not** in this public repository; keep them in a private folder (as `tests/README.md` does for the plan template).

### 1. Access OSP: single line diagram (PowerPoint, 4 samples)

- One line from homing to homing (FDU panel to FDU panel), through closures. **New is red, existing is blue**: dashed red line = new FOC, dashed blue = existing FOC; red pentagon = proposed closure, blue pentagon = existing closure; red box = new FDU panel, blue box = existing FDU panel.
- Site: name and code in bold beside its FDU (e.g. `SITE (CODE)`), and under it the FDU's block:
  - new FDU: `CODE_FDU_001`, `Capacity: 48 Ports`, `Terminated Ports: 1-48`, `Terminated Fibers: 13-60 (cable ID)`
  - existing FDU: `Capacity: 72 Ports`, `Active: 1-2,13-24`, `Vacant: 3-12,25-72`
- Proposed closure: `PROPOSED CLOSURE / STRAIGHT SPLICING / Coordinates: "TBF"` (coordinates in red). Existing closure: `EXISTING CLOSURE` and its coordinates. A photo of the existing closure and of each FDU sits above it.
- Each side of a closure carries its fibers in red: `F1-6 ⬠ F1-6` (straight), `F1-6 ⬠ F13-18` (new cable onto the vacant fibers of an existing one).
- Each cable: its cable ID under the line; a new one has its length in a green box (`30m`, `2km`, `1.2km`); an existing one reads `EXISTING 72 FOC`.
- The four cases: (1) a new link through proposed closures onto an existing cable; (2) a new site on a branch from a proposed closure, the branch carrying F1-6 to one side and F7-12 to the other; (3) a branch from a closure on an existing cable (F25-30 on both sides); (4) two legs (LEG 1, LEG 2) from two closures to one site.
- Legend at the foot; title block: logo, `SINGLE LINE DIAGRAM`, `PROJECT NAME_PLAN ID_SITENAME`, exchange, dwg. no., scale NTS, sheet no., issue date, three names over their roles, and a confidentiality line.

### 2. Broadband: splicing single line diagram (DXF)

- OLT → ODF (port groups `F1-F6`, `F7-F12`…) → splice points (SP1, SP2) where the 72C FOC fibers meet the 6F drop cables (`F2-F4 (72C FOC)` → `F2-F4 (6F DROP CABLE)`).
- One row per main / leg: `MAIN 1`, `LEG 01`, `[6FOC L001-L003 / F2-F4]`. Each line `Lnnn` is one fiber of the 72C (`F2-72C`) and the same fiber of the 6F drop (`F2-6C`); fiber 1 of each six is spare.
- Each NAP box: line ID, the 1:4 (circle) and 1:8 (triangles) symbols in green, `Lnnn_N01`, `16 ports`, `(n) pole ID`, pole type. The line's next NAP (`_N02`) hangs off it with `F1-F2`.
- Counts in a box: single LCP (lines), single NAP, double NAP, designed lines (= ports), demand lines.

### 3. Broadband: detailed splicing (DXF)

- ODF port list (used ports one by one, unused ones grouped) → **feeder 144C** → **144C closure** with `Fiber Splicing Assignment 13-44 (144C) / 13-44 (72C)` → **main distribution cables 72C** → **72C closures** (numbered) → **DROP 6F** cables through the NAPs.
- In a NAP box the six drop fibers run across. The line's fiber (highlighted yellow) goes into a **1:4**; outputs 3 and 4 feed the NAP's own **1:8**s (DNAP = two, 16 ports; SNAP = one, 8 ports); outputs 1 and 2 are spliced onto the drop's free fibers 1 and 2 and go on to the line's next NAP. Unused outputs are capped. Working fibers red, spare black.

## What the engine does

- **Access OSP**: from points (sites/FDU, closures, dummy NAPs), cables (size, new/existing, length, fibers in use) and **links** (two ends and the number of fibers), it finds each link's route and gives it, on every cable, **a run of free fibers inside one buffer** (the owner, 16 Nov: buffer first, the lowest spare only inside that rule): the lowest run of n free fibers in a row inside one buffer (n up to a buffer); for more, the lowest run from a buffer's first fiber; else n free fibers in one buffer, not in a row; only as a last result a run across buffers, said in a warning that names them. A cable's buffers hold 12 fibers, or 6 (`cable.fpt`, chosen on the cable card). Straight splices keep their numbers; an existing cable gives its first vacant fibers; a new FDU shared by two cables gives each an equal part of its ports, in whole buffers when every cable can have one (48 ports, three cables: 24 + 12 + 12). The FDU ports given to a new cable (on an existing FDU, or *Only what each leg uses*) are lined up with its buffers when the FDU has the room, so 6 + 12 fibers take F1-6 and F13-24, not F7-18; when the FDU is the limit, the warning says so. The samples reproduce the four PowerPoint cases (sample 2 gives exactly F1-6 / F7-12 on the branch and F13-18 on the existing cable).
- **Access OSP detailed** is drawn like the ODN's (owner's request): the homing ODF at the left with its working ports, every cable a bundle of fibers (the working ones one by one in red, the rest as two black lines), every closure an ellipse (red proposed, blue existing) with its splices inside and the fiber numbers at both ends, and the far ends at the right on rows of their own: an ODF (FDU panel) or a **dummy NAP** (pole-mounted small cell) instead of the ODN's NAPs. Every splice of the work is a **red dot** (layer `SPL_SPLICE_NEW`, ACI 1); a leg spliced only keeps a hollow red dot. The legend shows NEW SPLICE (and SPLICED ONLY, FOR FUTURE TESTING when used).
- **Fiber numbers everywhere** (both detailed drawings, owner's request): at every enclosure each splice shows its fiber on both sides (F25 into F1), the capped rest of each cable is named (F13-72), an ODF or dummy NAP row reads port and fiber (P25 F25), a 72C closure shows the main's fiber going in and the drop's fiber coming out, and each NAP shows the drop fibers 1-6 in and out and which fiber the line takes (F3 (6F) = F3 (72C)).
- **Broadband**: from the OLT/ODF, an optional feeder (size, closure, first fiber), the mains (size, closure, first fiber) and the NAPs (main, line, 8 or 16 ports, pole), it numbers the lines, fills 6F drops with five lines each (fibers 2-6), gives the mains their feeder fibers in order and wires each line's 1:4 and 1:8s. A line's next NAPs are fed on a 6F branch from its N01 (branch fibers 1, 2, 3 in order).
- **Broadband detailed** is one drawing in the layout of reference 3: the ODF at the lower left (this sheet's ports one by one), the feeder into its closure (an ellipse, the splices inside), each main as a bundle of fibers (working red, spare black) up to its 72C closure with its fiber splicing assignment, then every 6F drop, numbered 1, 2, 3…, through its N01s, the next NAPs hanging below on their branch. All the mains are in the one drawing. Its splices are red dots too: at the feeder closure, at each 72C closure (main fiber to drop fiber) and at the NAPs (the line's fiber into the 1:4, outputs 1 and 2 onto the branch, a branch fiber into the next NAP's 1:8).
- **Sheets**: A3 landscape, frame, title block (editable names and roles), legend. The single line diagram is one sheet.
- **Key map and grid sheets** (owner's request, "like a keymap + geo grids"): a detailed drawing whose smallest text (the fiber numbers) would print under about 1.8 mm (`model.grid = { text: 1.8 }`) is split like a map book. Sheet 1 is the **KEY MAP**: the whole drawing with a grid laid over its own extent, cells shaped like a sheet's drawing area, named A-01, B-01… (columns left to right, rows top to bottom); only the cells with something in them are drawn and get a sheet. Then one sheet per cell in reading order (SPLICING DETAILS · GRID B-01): the cell and a 4 % overlap enlarged to fill the drawing area, a dashed **match line** where a neighbour has a sheet (MATCH LINE · SEE C-01, with an arrow, in the overlap band), and a **locator** (a mini key map, this cell filled) in the legend band. The cutting is done in the engine on the primitives, so SVG, PDF and DXF agree: lines are cut at the window, fills cut to it, a circle partly out becomes cut lines, a text is kept whole on the sheet where most of it is (never cut); a long text across an edge widens that one sheet's view a little. A cell holding only what a neighbour's overlap already shows gets no sheet (its texts go to the neighbour); a cell whose drawing is a strip along a neighbour's edge (a sliver of a bundle, a closure's name) goes onto that neighbour's sheet, whose view grows to take it in as long as its fiber numbers still print at 90 % of the target or more (`model.grid.absorb`, 0.9); the key map outlines such a cell with SEE B-02. The lines of one label (a closure's three lines, a cable's name and WORKING line) always go on a sheet together. Of the grid placements tried (shifted in the room left over) the one with the fewest sheets wins, then the one that cuts the fewest closures, NAPs and ODFs and leaves the fewest sheets without a word, then the largest print. A closure, NAP or ODF that a sheet shows without its name gets its name again on that sheet, and a cable that runs a good way across a sheet without its label gets its label again (map-book style). A line that leaves a sheet where no neighbour has a sheet says where it goes on (CONTINUES ON D-01). The MATCH LINE labels stay off the texts, and the match lines break around them. The cells are named from the first column and row that have a sheet. The planner is bounded (at most 400 cells, a few passes; a label wider than most of a window widens only its own sheet). A drawing that already reads at that size on one sheet (enlarged to fit) stays one sheet, without a key map; `model.grid = false` forces one sheet as before. The demo pages name the sheets (Single line, Key map, A-01…) and a tap on a key map cell, the locator or a match line label (its target fills the overlap band) opens that sheet.
- **DXF**: R12 (AC1009), sheets side by side in model space, 1 unit = 1 mm, layers `SPL_FOC_NEW`, `SPL_FOC_EXIST`, `SPL_CLOSURE_NEW`, `SPL_SITE_NEW`, `SPL_FIBER`, `SPL_FIBER_USED`, `SPL_SPLITTER`, `SPL_NAP`, `SPL_CABLE`… with DASHED for cables.

## The owner's answers (15 Nov)

- Sample 3's new FDU: **Terminated Fibers 1-48** of the new branch cable. The reference's "13-60" was a slip copied from another drawing.
- An existing homing's FDU block (Active / Vacant) shows **the state before the work**. The new legs are shown by the fiber labels at the closures and by the legs' tags, not added to Active.
- Test details: in the **As-Built**, a tested leg carries its **test date and its loss / OTDR result**. (The As-Plan has no test result yet.)

## Plan for the app (chosen 15 Nov, after a study of the app and three designs)

**Ask & Draw.** A *Splicing details* page that opens full screen over the app, hosted like the CEF plan editor (its own page in a frame, with its own host object). The top of the screen is the single line diagram, drawn live by `splice.js`, so what the user sees is what prints. The bottom card asks one plain question at a time with big buttons. No tables and no typed fiber ranges.

- **Filled in from the project:** sites, FDUs (ODF records), closures (pole or handhole, ID, new/existing, coordinates, photo), dummy NAPs, the cables drawn in Route mode (size, new/existing, length), the names on the sheet. Data keyed by record id and cable `fid`, never by `RUN n` (those numbers move).
- **Asked:** where the new site's fibers go (one homing, a dummy NAP, or *Both*); how many fibers (6 already picked, 2 for a small cell); with two legs, **"Will both homings be tested end to end now?"** (*Yes, both / Only A / Only B*, nothing picked in advance); which ports are live at an existing FDU (tap or drag on a picture of the ports, *Same as the other homing*, *Not sure yet*); which buffers (tubes) of an existing cable are in use (asked once per cable, starting on a safe answer).
- **Worked out:** the way through the closures, every fiber number, the FDU ports. Anything can be changed by tapping it on the drawing; moving fibers uses a strip of coloured fiber dots, never typing. A "Still to answer: n" line counts down to *Ready · Export*.
- **Leg states** (on each leg, not on a cable, because one branch cable can carry both legs): *Tested end to end*, *Spliced only, test later* (fibers and ports kept for it), *Not built yet* (prints `xx-xx`). A spliced-only leg is drawn with a dashed fiber label box and the tag "SPLICED ONLY · FOR FUTURE TESTING"; on the detailed drawing its fibers are dashed with hollow splice dots. Later, *Mark tested* stamps the date and the loss / OTDR result (As-Built).
- **Steps:** (A) the engine: leg states, no routing through a site, one label per direction at a branch, separate ports per cable at an FDU, uncut fibers drawn passing through an existing closure, the FDU block as before the work; (B) the guided page with one way in (a Splicing button on the Drawing), Access OSP only; (C) tap-to-change, locks at the first export, Mark tested, Share merge; (D) the detailed drawing's details, photos on the PDF, homings off the map; (E) polish, tutorial, then Broadband.
- **Sizes (16 Nov):** the FDU card ("Capacity: 48 ports · Change": 12 · 24 · 48 · 72 · 144 · 288) and the cable card ("72C · new · 300 m · Change": 12 · 24 · 48 · 72 · 96 · 144 · 288, and *Other…* 2-576 for an existing cable; *Fibers per buffer: 12 · 6*), and a *Sizes* list on the Ready screen (every FDU, one row per cable RUN). A change edits the record itself: the ODF record's `boq.odf`, or the RUN's size and fibers per buffer (every piece), so the plan, the BOQ and the KMZ follow; a new site with no ODF record keeps its size question. Too small is said in red with what to pick, once on the Ready screen (a leg short only because of it is folded into it). Live ports past a smaller FDU, and buffers ticked in use past a smaller cable, stay in the answers but are left out of the plan and said in red (*Not live: remove …* / *Not in use: untick it*), so a wrong tap and the old size back by chip loses nothing; Undo brings the old size back.
- **The owner's choices (15 Nov):** fibers on an existing cable = the lowest free fiber (the references mix habits); `xx-xx (… LX)` = a possible second cable into the same new FDU, never on an existing one; the **As-Plan asks no testing questions and prints no testing words** — it only checks that there are free fibers on the actual existing footprint (live FDU ports, fibers in use), while the **As-Built** adds the leg states, the "tested now?" question and Mark tested (date, loss, OTDR); splitting a new FDU between two cables happens but not always, so it is asked when two cables end on one new FDU; cable IDs come later, so each prints `TBF` until entered, with a reminder that does not block export.

## Building it into the app

1. Build the model from the project, as above (done: see *In the app*).
2. Add the files to `sw.js`'s SHELL list (the APK copies `vendor/` whole: done), and change `VERSION` and, on beta, `APP_BETA` (the owner gives the number).

## In the app (beta)

- **Where:** the Drawing of an As-Plan or As-Built project. The round buttons on its right start with the two plans made from it, as icon buttons (the owner: icon mode): **CEF plan** (As-Plan, the tower) and **Splicing details** (the fiber join), each with a dot: green made, amber still to make or to finish (questions left, a size to fix). Their names are in `aria-label` and `title`. On the page, app mode turns the header, the stage chips and the main card actions into icon buttons (Done ✓, Undo, Your choices, A3 sheets, Next, Export…); the words stay where they are the content (a homing, a size, a format). The phone's Back closes a panel open on the page (the A3 sheets, Your choices, Export) before the page, and answers a question the app asks over it (Cancel) before anything closes. A site, an ODF, a closure or a dummy NAP tapped on the drawing offers **Splicing details ›** in its line. The page opens full screen in a frame (`#spliceSheet`), as the CEF plan does; **Done** or the phone's Back closes it.
- **The page:** `splice.html` loads `splice.js` and `ask.js` (in that order) and `ask.css`. `<html data-app="splice">` puts `ask.js` in its app mode: the project comes from `window.parent.__spliceHost`, nothing is kept in the browser's storage (the demo's key `gesaa-splice-ask-demo-1` is never touched), and opened by itself it says it needs the app. Without the attribute (`ask-demo.html`) it is the demo, unchanged.
- **The host** (`window.__spliceHost`, app.js, after the CEF section): `init()` gives the project (`spliceData`: the survey records without photos, the cable RUNs of Route with their size, family, fibers per buffer and cable ID, the title block as the plan's, the CEF sheets' three names), the saved answers, As-Plan or As-Built (the project's Purpose), the view-only text (an accepted task) and the record to show first; `save()`; `setOdfSize()`; `setRun()`; `deliver()` (the app's save and share, `noteExport('splice')`); `close()`.
- **`Ask.fromApp`** turns the app's data into the bridge's project: a Closure or dummy-NAP pin stands on the nearest pole of a cable (30 m, as the Drawing draws it); a closure or dummy NAP with no state is new; a pole's second box can be the dummy NAP; an ODF on a cable stands for its tower site (45 m), or is a homing itself with no site near (an exchange's FDU); a Service box can hold a closure; an OLT site is a plain point (Broadband comes later). Pieces are keyed by their cable and their two ends, so answers survive a RUN reversed or continued; answers about records or cables that are gone are pruned at load.
- **Storage:** `meta.splice = { v: 1, A: answers, tube, at, by, o, made }`, at most 200 000 characters of answers. The page saves only after a change made on it (opening and looking, or answers it tidied itself at load, write nothing), and a project's first save needs a started set; nothing is written when nothing changed. A typed cable ID not yet saved is saved when its field is left, the card closed, Done or Back. At a merge a set never started never replaces a started one. `A.tfpt` keeps the fibers per buffer each cable's ticked buffers were counted in: the RUN's `fpt` travels with the route, so when the two no longer match after a Share the ticked buffers are put in the RUN's buffers (live fibers stay live). A change cancels an on-site approval, except a save that only locks the fibers at an export. It travels with the project (Share, backup, the team mailbox): the one saved later is taken whole; Share's *Only the changes* counts it.
- **One source of truth for sizes:** the FDU size is written on the ODF record (`boq.odf`); a cable's size, fibers per buffer (`fpt: 6`, absent for 12) and cable ID (`cableId`, printed `<ID>-L1`, `-L2`… per piece) on its RUN, through Route's own write (the closures' sizes follow at once). Each of these three fields keeps its own time on the RUN (`ft: { size, fpt, cid }`, stamped by Route's write), so at a Share a field changed later on one phone is kept even when the other phone's RUN is newer as a whole. A site with two ODFs takes the size from, and writes it to, the ODF its cable leaves from. A pole with both a closure and a dummy NAP is drawn as the closure; the page says the dummy NAP is not drawn yet. A locked piece cut by a closure added later keeps its locked fibers on the new pieces. A new cable is offered only in the sizes the app has; a size of another family (a light cable to 24C) is asked first in the app. Undo writes the old value back.
- **The reminder:** opening the Drawing (bottom bar) of a project with a route that still has no CEF plan for a new tower site (As-Plan) or no splicing details: *Please create …*, with the two plan icons as big buttons (**Make the CEF plan**, **Make the splicing details**) and a quiet ✕ for **Later** (Esc and the phone's Back too); once per project each time the app is opened. Export the plan says it again in a soft box (*Still to make for this project*).
- **One PDF** (Export the plan; with Simple DXF the tile shows that it needs the company template and a tap leads to Plan settings): an icon tile with the three plans (the plan's sheets, the CEF plan's tower, the splicing details' join; a green dot when a plan is made, amber when not yet) and the caption *One PDF*. It makes one PDF: the plan's sheets of the drawing the Drawing shows (as *Also a PDF to print* draws them), then each tower site's CEF plan (its own PDF, made in the hidden frame as Export DXF's *Also the CEF plans*), then the splicing details (`Splice.build(model, ['sld', 'detailed'])` in the app's window: single line diagram, key map, grid sheets), put together with pdf-lib with a bookmark per part, and offered in the result box (the website's download or Share, the Android app's Documents or share sheet). A plan not made yet, or splicing details not finished (questions left, a cable with no type, a size too small, a leg short of fibers), is asked first: **Make it now** (the editor opens over Export; at Done the tile is shown again) or **Export without it**. The export issues the splicing details: their fibers lock as the page's Export locks them (`Ask.locks`, shared by both), saved without cancelling an approval; an accepted (view-only) task is exported as it is, with no question. Export DXF and its ZIP are unchanged.
